newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes up, Dec Dubai done at full/mth +47.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes up, Dec Dubai done at full/mth +47.

text.p: Crude oil prices edged up in Asia on Thursday, with further Oman deals emerging from late last week.
Traders said a major sold its remaining Oman into the Far East market at MPM premiums as high as 13 cents per barrel.
One of the buyers, a South Korean refiner, aquired up to two million barrels from the major for December lifting.

Some players had indicated the major was holding the barrels to bolster term talks covering 1997, but the deals indicate that it had sold barrels even before heading to South Korea and onto Japan for term talks.
Nov paper Tapis was assessed 20/30 cents up in little talk as trading has already moved forward into December.
December Tapis paper was quoted at $22.85/$23.00 per barrel, up 20 cents from Wednesday. Traders exchanged 50,000 barrels of December Tapis on paper at $23.00, brokers said.

A major sold a wet Dec Dubai at full-month quotes +47 cents. Crude term talks with ADNOC over Murban were underway with price views ranging +25 to +30 cents, traders said. Stasco's Oman term talks continued with the major said to be offering term at +12 cents. --Singapore, N. Fullick (+65 870 3081), Tokyo, M. Yoshikawa (+813-5473 3706)
Traders said there was talk a December Kutubu was sold by a major at Tapis quotes plus 27 cents per barrel, but some traders said this might be an old deal coming back into the market.
Elsewhere, traders said December premium for Minas and Widuri -- the most likely crudes to be displaced by incoming West African grades -- were holding.
But, with most of the 3-4 million barrels of West African crude lifting in December, Indonesia crude sellers were bracing themselves for pressure on the January premium.
For the time being, Widuri was talked around 40 cents per barrel over the ICP and Minas around 45 cents per barrel.
